scope: Isolated self-hosted PostgreSQL-backed Temporal with mTLS/JWT namespace authorization and actual worker containers; no production cutover
checks: Actual PostgreSQL-backed Temporal service accepts trusted mTLS and signed namespace-scoped JWT credentials
A namespace reader cannot start workflows; a tampered signed JWT is rejected before execution
Temporal's default authorizer rejects another namespace, expired JWT and invalid JWT on real namespace RPCs
Real TLS handshake rejects missing/untrusted client certificates and incorrect server hostname without bypassing verification
Signing-key rotation permits the replacement credential and rejects the removed key on actual Temporal RPCs
Actual worker container reads the authenticated private fixture through its configured provider route
25 held plans and 50 concurrent transfer calls persist exactly 25 intents without effects
Packaged scheduler SIGKILL and replacement drain persisted backlog using natural lease expiry, without new intents
All 25 workflows have one start event; held approvals remain effect-free under bounded worker concurrency
Local readiness and backlog metrics recover and expose no workload credential
Actual database connection interruption makes both packaged roles unready; held work preserves action IDs and zero effects
First replacement startup with database still unavailable terminates both actual processes without effects; supervisor retries only terminal children
Database connectivity restoration and supervisor replacement resume the same 25 histories without approval bypass or replacement actions
Actual Temporal service and persistence PostgreSQL SIGKILL/restart retain all 25 histories, exact action IDs and held approvals
Replacement worker container retains authenticated provider connectivity after injected recovery faults
Packaged pinned worker SIGKILL and restart preserves pending work; exact approval completes one CRM and one email
Restoring a pre-effect Temporal PostgreSQL backup reopens history; durable LoopLabs completion prevents duplicate CRM/email effects
Other stale shared-contact runs are contained without duplicate effects or downstream sends
Workload revocation makes both packaged roles unready
limitations: One laptop sample, not capacity, percentile latency or availability SLO
25 concurrent held runs; one approved completion; remaining shared-contact plans contained
Single-node service/persistence SIGKILL and quiesced Temporal backup restore; no LoopLabs database restore, replicated failover or availability SLA
Local Docker mTLS/JWT cluster only; no remote managed-cluster acceptance, SSO or independent security audit
No hosted atomic CRM guarantee or real provider delivery
